comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the theoretical efficiency improvements (C2, C3, C8, C42, C64) well-supported by mathematical modeling showing 80-92% improvement. Peer reviewers confirm 'convincing results' and 'solid evidence' for the theoretical advantages.

Strong agreement on success rates. Both evaluations support the reported experimental data (C4, C5, C46-C50) and comparisons to literature. OpenEval notes sample size differences (33 vs 136 attempts) while peer reviewers accept the results without challenge, confirming 'convincing results' and successful recording rates.

Significant disagreement on connectivity findings. OpenEval supports the experimental data and probabilistic analysis (C6, C7, C55-C61) as appropriately contextualized. However, Peer Reviewer 3 raises substantial concerns about the low 5% connectivity rate, suggesting the system may not reliably detect close-proximity connections and questioning whether biological variation (C77, C78) adequately explains the findings.

Disagreement on comparative context. OpenEval finds the timing and performance metrics (C52, C53, C54) well-supported as direct measurements. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'a comparison of measurements shown in Figure 2 to other methods has not been addressed adequately,' indicating insufficient comparative evidence for efficiency claims.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations support the technical apparatus description (C43, C87-C105) as comprehensive and adequate for reproducibility. Peer reviewers note the implementation is 'useful' and 'economically favourable' without challenging any technical details.

Strong agreement on methods. Both evaluations support the experimental protocols (C106-C118 for OpenEval; C51, C107-C118 for peer). Peer reviewers accept the methodology while requesting additional discussion of cell type identification, but do not challenge the core protocols.

Agreement on algorithmic approach. Both evaluations support the patch-walking algorithm description (C119-C139 for OpenEval; C119-C133 for peer). Peer reviewers acknowledge the 'coordinated pipette route-planning' and 'fully automated' approach without challenging the implementation.

Disagreement on quality control. OpenEval finds the QC criteria (C144-C146) and connectivity testing (C147-C151) appropriately described and consistent with literature. Peer Reviewer 2 raises critical concerns that 'cells with Access Resistance >40 MOhm appear to still be included,' suggesting criteria may not have been consistently applied.

Significant disagreement on practical advantages. OpenEval supports claims about reduced tissue damage, time savings, and method advantages (C65-C68) as logical inferences. Peer reviewers express substantial concerns: Reviewer 2 notes 'discussion of implementation to manual methods is still lacking,' and Reviewer 3 states 'overall applicability seems limited' with loss of morphological information.

Partial overlap with disagreement. OpenEval supports accessibility and utility claims (C72, C73, C76, C86) as reasonable conclusions, though notes speculation about time reduction. Peer reviewers question these claims more strongly, with Reviewer 2 noting lack of comparison to manual methods and Reviewer 3 expressing concerns about limited applicability and loss of morphological data.

Agreement on future directions with caveats. OpenEval supports the scaling cautions and future recommendations (C69-C71) as reasonable. Peer reviewers also accept these as reasonable proposals, with Reviewer 1 noting 'important practical technical considerations,' though Reviewer 3 cautions about 'significant technical and logistical complexities' in scaling.

Agreement on speculative extensions. OpenEval supports future directions (C80-C85) as appropriately speculative proposals with relevant citations. Peer reviewers similarly accept these as reasonable future work, with acknowledgment of limitations in scalability.

Agreement on uncertainty. Both evaluations express uncertainty about the biological variation explanation (C77, C78). OpenEval notes the explanation is 'explicitly speculative' without supporting data. Peer Reviewer 3 suggests alternative explanations related to spatial limitations of the system rather than biological variation.

Agreement on observational data. OpenEval supports the brain region data (C51) and connection observations (C62, C63) as directly reported with appropriate qualification. Peer reviewers accept these findings, confirming detection of synaptic connections and acknowledging technical challenges through spatial restriction concerns.

Agreement on technical challenges. OpenEval supports the tissue deformation observation (C79) as an important documented limitation. Peer reviewers implicitly acknowledge this through Reviewer 3's concerns about spatial restrictions and the need for greater neuron separation.

Agreement on baseline data. OpenEval supports the uncoordinated experimental baseline (C44, C45) as appropriate contextualization. Peer reviewers accept these comparisons as part of the overall success rate data without specific challenge.
